summary.headline: Pritika Auto Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31.55% YoY to Rs 153.19 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 13.85% from 15.99%.
summary.overview: Consolidated net revenue from operations was Rs 153.19 crore in Q2 FY27 versus Rs 116.45 crore a year earlier, up 31.55%, with production volumes up about 22% to 15,665 metric tons. EBITDA margin was 13.85%, down from 15.99% a year ago but up from 13.45% in Q1 FY27, which management attributed to volatile raw material (scrap) prices. Management reported a new export order from Italy via subsidiary Pritika Engineering Components and Kion USA product approval with production expected in FY28. Management guided to 15-20% annual growth and a 14-15% margin, and targets 1 lakh metric tons of capacity by calendar 2028.

segments.name: Pritika Auto Industries (standalone/core)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue growth quoted at 13.97% to Rs 21.21 crore vs Rs 18.61 crore; the figure is ambiguous in the transcript and may refer to a segment or standalone line. Commentary says 7% of business comes from commercial vehicles.

segments.name: Pritika Engineering Components (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Secured a high-value export order from an Italian precision engineering manufacturer, approx. 12 crore per annum initially, with potential to reach Rs 40-50 crore in about three years. Capacity utilisation share cited at 23-25%, targeted to rise to 30-35%.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth target of 15-20% YoY over the coming years.
EBITDA margin target of 14-15%, with expected uplift from LFC (lost foam casting) ramp-up; management said margins to improve gradually and sequential improvement expected in Q3.
Q3 expected to be seasonally lower than Q2 for tractor and general industry due to planned maintenance in December.
Capacity to reach 80,000 MT with an additional 7,800 MT ready by end of November 2026; a further 24,000 MT planned on acquired land, taking capacity to 1 lakh MT by calendar 2028.
Railway components: RDSO submissions targeted by Jan-Feb 2027, with supply expected from Sep-Oct 2027.
Kion USA: regular production expected to start in FY28; management hopes it becomes a major US customer within 2-3 years.

Solar power MoU (Aug 2026) with Spark Grid for 25+ years; group savings about Rs 110 crore, with about Rs 70 crore to Pritika Engineering and Mahindra-linked entity Mitha Casting and the balance to Pritika Auto. Pritika Engineering to hold 26% in the proposed SPV.
capex_capacity: Green sand capacity utilisation at about 90%; lost foam casting (LFC) capacity at about 50%.
Green sand capacity expansion of about 600 (units as stated) with the first 7,800 MT addition ready by end of November 2026.
Plan to add 24,000 MT on newly acquired land, with construction through 2027 and full 1 lakh MT by calendar 2028.
Automation: fettling automation machines being procured; robotics and gantry systems planned in machine shop for high-volume parts to reduce manpower cost.
Funding of expansion to be a mix of debt (major part) and equity; management said consolidated net debt to equity was about 0.67 and debt position is comfortable.
demand_pricing: Export: Italian order of approx. 12 crore per annum; management sees potential to Rs 40-50 crore within about three years.
Demand supported by existing OEMs (Mahindra, Swaraj, Tafe, Sonalika, Escorts Kubota, CNH); repeat and incremental business reported.
Raw material: scrap is the main input; steel and scrap price increases were passed through to customers with a one-quarter lag, which hit Q2 margins.
Product mix shift toward large castings (for example, a 530 kg casting developed via LFC, previously imported from China) with higher value realisation and fewer competitors.
Industry: management says the tractor business is largely domestic and insulated from geopolitical shocks; farmers benefited from better pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Export growth potential and target contribution to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Italian order could scale from 12 crore per annum to Rs 40-50 crore within about three years; no firm export-share percentage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue grow 31% while the margin fell about 200 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin pressure to sharp raw material (scrap) price increases that are passed through with about a one-quarter lag, so margins are expected to improve next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion utilisation and return profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Green sand capacity is about 90% utilised and LFC about 50%. Subsidiary capacity share is around 23-25%, targeted to reach 30-35%. Funding mix is mostly debt with some equity.

qa_highlights.question: Railway and HCV opportunity timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Two or three railway components are being developed for RDSO approval by Jan-Feb 2027, with supply targeted from Sep-Oct 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses and interest cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increases are in line with growth and that interest as a percentage of revenue has declined.

qa_highlights.question: Why have ROA and net debt-to-equity fluctuated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt was taken last year to fund growth, and the company is now raising both debt and equity for expansion; net debt to equity was stated as 0.67.

risks_watch: Raw material (scrap) price volatility and the one-quarter pass-through lag, which compressed Q2 margins.
Sequential Q3 seasonality: December planned maintenance and tractor-cycle softness may reduce volumes.
Capacity build-out to 1 lakh MT by 2028 depends on land acquisition and debt-led funding; leverage (net debt to equity 0.67 cited) may rise.
Timing of Kion USA commercial production (FY28) and railway RDSO approvals; execution on the Italian order.
Transcript quality is poor in places (figures such as ROA, H1 EBITDA margin and capacity increments may be misreported). Verify against the investor presentation before relying on them.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, exports and capacity plans, with specific timelines. Noticeably less precise on margin drivers and balance-sheet questions, where answers were brief and deflected to seasonality and pass-through mechanics.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin 13.85% in Q2 FY27 vs 13.45% in Q1 and 15.99% a year ago; management says scrap pass-through lag hit Q2 and sequential improvement is expected in Q3, with medium-term target 14-15%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: First 7,800 MT green sand addition ready by end-November 2026, taking capacity to 80,000 MT; green sand utilisation at about 90%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Production volume up 22% YoY to 15,665 MT in Q2 and 19% in H1 to 30,000 MT, with the 7,800 MT addition coming online; but Q3 guided lower than Q2 on December maintenance.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Green sand at about 90% utilisation and a 24,000 MT expansion planned on newly acquired land, with debt-led funding already being arranged; formal capex figure not yet disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held 15-20% revenue growth and 14-15% margin guidance, with the margin target cut from earlier levels and no raise signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 margin of 13.85% sits below the 14-15% target, Q3 is guided seasonally lower, and scrap price volatility is unresolved.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Kion USA regular production expected to start in FY28, and railway components have RDSO submissions targeted by Jan-Feb 2027 with supply from Sep-Oct 2027.

rows.label: Italian export order scaling
rows.why: Italian order worth about Rs 12 crore per annum initially, with potential to Rs 40-50 crore in about three years; subsidiary utilisation share 23-25% targeted to 30-35%.

rows.label: Railway components via RDSO approval
rows.why: Two or three railway components in development, RDSO submissions targeted by Jan-Feb 2027, but approval is not yet secured.

rows.label: Solar PPA savings
rows.why: Solar power MoU (Aug 2026) with Spark Grid for 25+ years; group savings about Rs 110 crore, with about Rs 70 crore to Pritika Engineering and the balance to Pritika Auto, subject to SPV formation.

tone.note: Management was confident on exports, capacity timelines and the 15-20% growth target, but brief and deflecting on the margin drop and balance-sheet questions, where analysts pressed on the 200 bps QoQ margin fall and rising leverage.
